text: Complex differentiability at a point is a strictly stronger condition than real differentiability of the corresponding map from R^2 to R^2.
explanation: True: complex differentiability adds the Cauchy-Riemann constraints on top of real differentiability, forcing the Jacobian to act as multiplication by a complex number (a rotation and scaling). This rigidity is why analytic functions are automatically infinitely differentiable, with no real-variable analogue.
